newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
RAO ARRESTED, RELEASED ON BAIL

Former Prime Minister Narasimha Rao was arrested in the St Kitts forgery case and released on bail. The non-bailable warrant orders earlier issued by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate of Delhi were executed by two officials belonging to the Central Bureau of Investigaton. Prior to his arrest, Rao had secured temporary anticipatory bail from the Delhi High Court in the St Kitts case until October 14.
Indian Express
UTTAR PRADESH HEADING FOR HUNG ASSEMBLY

Uttar Pradesh is heading for a hung Assembly with no party likely to secure majority in the 425-member Assembly. According to trends in 327 constituencies, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was ahead in 130 seats, United Front (UF) combine in 104 followed by the Congress-Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) alliance in 84. Out of results for 25 seats declared so far, BJP won 15 seats. BSP-Congress alliance and UF bagged five seats each.
The Economic Times
TATAS TACKLING TAKEOVER THREATS

A recent rights issue by the Tata group's holding company, Tata Sons, to various group companies is aimed at consolidating its control over the group and ward off takeover threats. According to group chairman Ratan Tata a stronger Tata Sons would ensure that it guided the group and shaped its future plans. Tata Sons would act as a central entity, like Tata Industries, for promoting ventures strategic to group's growth, he said.
INDUSTRY PESSIMISTIC ON SECOND HALF OF CURRENT FISCAL

The business community is worried that the second half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) may be worse than the first half. The decline in Business Confidence Index (BCI) reflected the pessimism in the corporate sector. From 124.7 in December 1995, BCI fell to 103.4 in August this year. According to economists, the main factor behind the industry's negative assessment of country's economic environment was the high cost of money.
Financial Express
AVIATION MINISTER'S POLICY STATEMENT COMES UNDER FIRE

Civil Aviation minister C.M. Ibrahim's announcement prohibiting foreign equity participation in domestic airlines has come under fire. Four major ministries, including Finance, External Affairs, Industry and Commerce, have taken strong exception to the premature policy announcement. They have reportedly asked the civil aviation minister to clarify on the issue. The policy on foreign equity investment in domestic airlines is said to have been announced without prior approval of the Cabinet.
B.A.T. TRYING TO RAISE STAKE IN ITC

UK based B.A.T. Industries Plc, the largest single shareholder in ITC Ltd, has placed a purchase order for around 700,000 shares of the company. At an average price of around 300 rupees per share, the order works out to around 210 million rupees. The purchase order is seen as part of BAT's long-term strategy to hike its stake in ITC from the current level of 32 percent.
POLITICAL UNCERTAINTY AFFECTING MARKETS

Faith in India's ability to attract foreign investors has come under a cloud following the current slump in stock markets. It is feared that country's viability as an emerging market may fast erode in the face of political uncertainty and amidst worries regarding possible reversal of market reforms. According to several foreign fund managers, domestic funds and retail investors were shunning the market, raising a scare among foreign investors.
Business Standard
FOREIGN INVESTMENT WILL REMAIN CYCLICAL

According to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the stock market regulator, the capital market may continue to witness a cyclical trend for investments by foreign institutional investors (FII) over the next 12 months. As on September 30, 1996, figures on net FII investments at the stock markets stood at $122.8 million, said SEBI. Cumulative investment by FIIs currently stood at $6.79 billion, SEBI said.
INDIA TAKES PRIME SLOT IN PEPSICO'S BUSINESS RECAST

PepsiCo India's beverage business is set to be converted into an independent strategic business unit reporting directly to PepsiCo's headquarters in New York. The move is part of a major international restructuring in the company, now being given a final shape. Apart from India, Russia and China also figure as the multinational's special business units.
PRIME HAZIRA TO PICK UP 49 PCT STAKE IN ESSAR POWER

The Mauritius-based Ruia company, Prime Hazira, is set to become the single-largest shareholder in Essar Power, currently fully owned by the Essar group controlled by the Ruia family. Prime Hazira has picked up 178 million new shares issued by Essar Power for 10 rupees per share. This amounted to 40 percent of Essar Power's enhanced equity of 4.45 billion rupees. Prime Hazira plans to pick up another nine percent in Essar Power once it receives necessary government approvals.
TWO NEW FOREIGN EXCHANGE DERIVATIVES FOR FIRMS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced two new exotic derivative instruments in the Indian foreign exchange market. RBI has allowed the corporates to sell and authorised dealers to offer risk-effective option strategies like range forwards and ratio range forward to their customers. These new derivatives can be offered if there is no net inflow of premium to them, the central bank has ruled.
Business Line
INFRASTRUCTURE REQUIREMENT ESTIMATED AT $130 BLN

India's infrastructure investment could rise from current $17 billion a year to about $30 billion by the year 2,001, says an official paper. It says India's total infrastructure fund requirement over the next five years will be around $115-$130 billion. These may touch $215 billion in the following five years. The funds requirement for the power sector has been put at 1500 billion rupees for raising the capacity by an additional 50,000 megawatts (MW) to 60,000 MW. In telecommunication, the requirement is expected to be around 1400 billion rupees.
